A1_atp_watch.title: Kavach watches speed and signals, warns, then brakes

cues.vo: Kavach is India's own Automatic Train Protection system. It watches the train's speed and the signals ahead, and if the train goes too fast or is about to pass a red signal, it warns the loco pilot... then brakes by itself if nothing changes.

A1_atp_watch.spec: A WAP-7-style electric loco (generic, no livery text) hauling a short rake on a 3D ballasted track at dusk; camera orbits from 3/4 front. Floating cab-display telemetry (cyan) above the cab: PERMITTED SPEED and the next signal with its distance. On 'too fast or is about to pass a red signal' the signal ahead turns red and the telemetry flashes amber WARNING; on 'then brakes by itself' a cyan pulse runs from the Kavach unit into the brake pipe, brake blocks glow, sparks, the speed dial needle drops. Label AUTOMATIC TRAIN PROTECTION. Tag: ILLUSTRATION.

A2_four_links.title: A chain of four links

cues.vo: It looks like magic on video. But Kavach is a chain of four links, and it only protects you when every link is in place.

A2_four_links.spec: The train from A1 in a dark void; four glowing cyan chain links assemble around it one by one, each tied to its place (track sleeper, station building, radio tower, loco cab). On 'every link is in place' the chain closes and the whole rig lights. Keep the four positions: they return in A9. Tag: ILLUSTRATION.

A3_rfid_tags.title: Link one: RFID tags on the sleepers

cues.vo: Link one sits on the track — small R-F-I-D tags fixed to the concrete sleepers, which a reader under the engine reads as it passes, so the train knows exactly where it is and on which line.

A3_rfid_tags.spec: Low tracking shot along concrete (PSC) sleepers; a yellow-black RFID tag box between the rails; the loco's under-chassis reader (X-ray view through the bogie) passes over it, a radio field ring lights the tag, and two small chips pop: TAG ID and TRACK ID, then a map pin snaps onto the line ('exactly where it is and on which line'). Label LINK 1 · RFID TAG. Tag: ILLUSTRATION.

A4_station_interlock.title: Link two: station Kavach reads interlocking

cues.vo: Link two is the station. A Kavach computer there reads the signals, the points and which tracks are occupied, straight from the station's own signalling system — called interlocking. Remember that word.

A4_station_interlock.spec: Station cutaway: a relay room / interlocking cabinet and a Kavach cabinet beside it; live wires carry signal aspects (red/yellow/green), point positions and track-occupied states into the Kavach box as flowing light. On 'called interlocking' the word INTERLOCKING lights on the cabinet and stays lit; a slow push-in on it for 'Remember that word'. Label LINK 2 · INTERLOCKING. Tag: ILLUSTRATION.

A5_radio_tower.title: Link three: UHF safety radio

cues.vo: Link three is the radio. Tall towers along the line carry messages between the station and the engine over a U-H-F safety radio... it's not your mobile network, and it's not five G.

A5_radio_tower.spec: Tilt up a lattice telecom tower beside the track at night; radio pulses (cyan rings) travel between the station, the tower and the moving loco. On 'it's not your mobile network, and it's not five G' a phone-network badge and a 5G badge float in and grey out. Label LINK 3 · UHF DATA RADIO. Tag: ILLUSTRATION.

A6_loco_xray.title: Link four: the loco unit, exploded

cues.vo: And link four rides inside the engine — a Kavach computer, R-F-I-D readers, wheel speed sensors, a screen for the loco pilot, and a link to the brakes.

A6_loco_xray.spec: The loco shell peels away layer by layer (X-ray, cyan edges): each part lights and labels in on its word: KAVACH COMPUTER, RFID READERS (under the bogie), WHEEL SPEED SENSORS (on the axle), CAB SCREEN, BRAKE LINK. Label LINK 4 · LOCO KAVACH. Tag: ILLUSTRATION.

A7_info_arrow.title: Kavach acts only on the information it is given

cues.vo: So keep this one in your pocket... Kavach can only act on the information it's given.

breaks.note: chapter card THE PHYSICS (end of block 1)

A7_info_arrow.spec: The four-link rig, wide: a single data arrow travels from the station interlocking into the Kavach box and glows; the camera holds on it while everything else dims. Ends on a slow dim to black (chapter card follows). Tag: ILLUSTRATION.

A8_brake_pipe.title: Low grip, heavy train, brake pipe

cues.vo: Because steel wheels on a steel rail have very little grip, a train is enormously heavy, and when the brakes go on, the air pressure has to change all the way down the brake pipe to the last coach.

A8_brake_pipe.spec: Macro of a steel wheel on a steel rail (the tiny contact patch glows), then pull back along a long rake; on 'when the brakes go on' an air-pressure wave travels down the brake pipe coach by coach (cyan → amber as it goes) to the last coach. Label BRAKE PIPE. Tag: ILLUSTRATION.

A9_links_relight.title: Kavach needs four things

cues.vo: Kavach isn't magic, and it isn't useless. It's an Indian-built safety layer that brakes early when a human slips... as long as the engine is fitted, the track section is working, the signalling data is right, and there's enough room to stop.

A9_links_relight.spec: The rig from A2 at dawn light: on the four phrases the links relight one by one: ENGINE (loco cab), TRACK (sleepers), DATA (interlocking), DISTANCE (a braking ruler drawn ahead of the train). On-screen `ENGINE · TRACK · DATA · DISTANCE` as four small labels at their links. Tag: ILLUSTRATION.

B1_braking_ruler.title: Vande Bharat: 654 m from 130 km/h

cues.vo: Here's a real number from the railway's own training notes. A Vande Bharat running at one hundred and thirty kilometres per hour needs about six hundred and fifty metres to stop... even with its emergency brakes.
cues.onscreen: VANDE BHARAT · 130 KM/H · EMERGENCY BRAKE 654 M

B1_braking_ruler.spec: Side-on train silhouette (Vande Bharat nose shape, no livery text) runs left to right over a track ruler; on 'about six hundred and fifty metres' the brake point fires and a speed-vs-distance curve draws from 130 KM/H to 0 along a 0–700 m ruler, landing at 654 M. Leave the first ~4 s for a document insert (coordinator overlays the IRIMEE table); keep motion behind it. On-screen `VANDE BHARAT · 130 KM/H · EMERGENCY BRAKE 654 M`.

B2_curve_stretch.title: 130 → 160 km/h: about half again

cues.vo: And if you push the speed from one hundred and thirty to one hundred and sixty, the braking distance doesn't grow by a little... it grows by about half.

B2_curve_stretch.spec: The B1 curve (130 km/h) stays as a ghost; a second curve from 160 km/h draws and stretches about 1.5× as far; a bracket labels +50%. Generic distances (no metres on this one), amber for the longer curve. On-screen `+50%`. Tag: ILLUSTRATIVE CURVE.

B3_fog_split.title: Fog: 50 m in about 1.6 s

cues.vo: Suppose the loco pilot can see a signal only fifty metres ahead. At one hundred and ten kilometres per hour, the train crosses those fifty metres in less than two seconds — and even an alert person needs a second or two just to react. On eyes alone, the maths simply doesn't work.

B3_fog_split.spec: Split screen. Left: windscreen view into dense fog (procedural fog over a param plate `fog.mp4` if supplied, else a layered fog shader), a signal emerges at 50 m; a stopwatch races and runs out at 1.6 s as the train passes it. Right half stays dark until B4. On 'needs a second or two just to react' a reaction bar fills; on 'On eyes alone' a red cross. On-screen `VISIBILITY 50 M · EXAMPLE · ≈ 1.6 S`. Tag: ILLUSTRATION.

B4_kavach_curve.title: Kavach knows the signal ahead and brakes early

cues.vo: This is where Kavach changes the game. It doesn't wait for anyone to see the red signal — it already knows how far away it is, shows it on the screen inside the cab, and if the loco pilot doesn't slow down, brakes early while there's still enough room.

B4_kavach_curve.spec: Right half of the split lights: the cab display (LP-OCIP grammar: target distance counting down, permitted speed, signal aspect) shows the red signal long before it is visible; then a full-width braking curve draws ahead of the train with the Kavach brake point well before the signal and the stop short of it. On-screen `TARGET DISTANCE`. Tag: ILLUSTRATION.

B5_cant_cancel_physics.title: Danger inside the stopping distance

cues.vo: But it can't cancel physics. If danger appears closer than the stopping distance, even Kavach can't stop the train in time.

B5_cant_cancel_physics.spec: The curve from B4; an obstacle appears inside the curve's reach; the zone between obstacle and stop point washes crimson; the curve cannot bend in time. No label needed. Tag: ILLUSTRATION.

B6_spad_counter.title: 208 red-signal passings, 12 collisions

cues.vo: And how often does a train pass a red signal by mistake? The Commission of Railway Safety noted two hundred and eight such cases in five years, from April twenty nineteen to March twenty twenty four... and twelve of them ended in a collision.

B6_spad_counter.spec: A red signal lamp at night (graphic); a counter rolls 0 → 208 across a timeline APR 2019 → MAR 2024 (each case a small tick); on 'twelve of them' 12 ticks turn crimson and pulse. Leave room upper half for a document insert the coordinator may overlay. On-screen `208 CASES · 2019–2024 · 12 COLLISIONS`.

C1_balasore_layout.title: Bahanaga Bazar: green for the main line, crossover to the loop

cues.vo: Case one. Bahanaga Bazar, near Balasore in Odisha, June two, twenty twenty three. The Coromandel Express is coming in at about one hundred and twenty eight kilometres per hour, on a green signal for the main line.
But the crossover ahead is set towards the loop line... where a goods train is standing.

C1_balasore_layout.spec: Top-down 2.5D station schematic (not a map trace): up main line, loop line with a parked goods train, crossover 17A/B, the home signal. V040: the Coromandel arrow approaches on the up main (≈ 128 KM/H readout) and the home signal turns green. V041: the crossover points swing towards the loop; the parked goods train highlights crimson. Leave the first ~3 s for archive the coordinator cuts in. On-screen `BAHANAGA BAZAR · 2 JUN 2023 · ≈ 128 KM/H`, then `CROSSOVER 17A/B → LOOP`. Tag: ILLUSTRATION.

C2_would_kavach.title: So, would Kavach have stopped it?

cues.vo: So, would Kavach have stopped it?

breaks.note: 1.5 s total music silence, then a low braam on 'the honest answer' (core reveal)

C2_would_kavach.spec: The C1 schematic frozen; a cyan Kavach box appears on the loco and pulses slowly. Includes the 1.5 s total silence: keep it still but alive (slow pulse, drifting dust). Ends on a cut.

C3_false_green.title: Same wrong input, same answer

cues.vo: Remember interlocking? At Balasore, the signalling system itself was showing a false green, and fed that same wrong information, Kavach could have believed the line was clear too.
A safety computer can't correct wrong information it trusts. Kavach does have a few checks of its own, but no public study has shown whether they would have acted in time there.

C3_false_green.spec: V045: the interlocking feed lights; the false green travels down the wire into the Kavach box, which shows green too (`SAME INPUT · SAME ANSWER?`). V046: two parallel safety channels inside Kavach both agree on the wrong input and a gate opens; then dotted, uncertain tag-read marks appear on the loop line (`UNTESTED COUNTERFACTUAL`). Tag: ILLUSTRATION.

C4_signals_fail.title: Rangapani: automatic signals failed

cues.vo: Case two. Rangapani, near New Jalpaiguri in north Bengal, June seventeen, twenty twenty four. The automatic signals had failed, so trains had to move on a paper authority, at a slow, careful speed.

C4_signals_fail.spec: A line of automatic signals along a single track blinks out one by one (power-down); a generic paper authority slip (no copy of a real form, just a blank slip with a stamp shape) slides in; trains shown as slow arrows. Leave the first ~3 s for archive. On-screen `RANGAPANI · 17 JUN 2024 · SIGNALS FAILED`. Tag: ILLUSTRATION.

C5_wrong_form.title: Wrong form, no caution order, missing walkie-talkies, training

cues.vo: The inquiry found the goods train was handed the wrong form, T-A nine one two instead of T-D nine one two, with no caution order, missing walkie talkies, and training that wasn't good enough... failures of the system, not just one loco pilot.

C5_wrong_form.spec: Two distinct form labels T/A 912 and T/D 912 side by side; the wrong one (T/A 912) is handed to the goods train arrow and highlights crimson. Then three items tick crimson around the station: CAUTION ORDER, WALKIE-TALKIES, TRAINING. On-screen `T/A 912 ≠ T/D 912`. Tag: ILLUSTRATION.

C6_speed_trace.title: 78 km/h, hit at about 40

cues.vo: The goods train reached seventy eight kilometres per hour and hit the Kanchanjunga Express from behind at about forty. And there was no working Kavach on that section.

C6_speed_trace.spec: Speed-vs-time trace for the goods train climbs to 78, then the collision marker at about 40 behind the passenger train; a schematic map strip shows no Kavach line on this section. On-screen `78 KM/H → ≈ 40 KM/H · NO KAVACH HERE`. Tag: ILLUSTRATION.

C7_rewind_sim.title: With Kavach: held to a slow speed

cues.vo: Here, Kavach could have made a real difference. With both trains fitted and the section working, it could have held the goods train to the allowed movement and a slow speed past those failed signals.

C7_rewind_sim.spec: The C6 scene rewinds (tape-rewind feel); a cyan Kavach box appears on both locos; the goods train's speed is held low past the failed signals and its braking curve stops it short of the passenger train. On-screen `SIMULATION` (small, in-scene; the assembler also tags it).

C8_two_failures.title: Two crashes, two failures

cues.vo: Two crashes, two different failures. At Balasore the signalling information itself was wrong, at Kanchanjunga the backup rules broke down — and Kavach is strongest against the second kind.

breaks.note: chapter card WHAT YOU CAN DO, warm music returns

C8_two_failures.spec: Two columns: left WRONG INPUT (a crimson false green feeding a box), right BROKEN BACKUP (dark signals and a torn paper slip); on 'Kavach is strongest against the second kind' the right column gets a cyan shield. On-screen `WRONG INPUT · BROKEN BACKUP`.

D1_tag_spacing.title: Max gap 1 km; 2,872 tags on 96 km

cues.vo: People say there's one tag every kilometre. Actually, one kilometre is only the longest gap allowed — near signals, points and stations the tags crowd together, and on one stretch of about ninety six kilometres between Vadodara and Ahmedabad, the railway fixed two thousand eight hundred and seventy two of them.

D1_tag_spacing.spec: First half: evenly spaced dots along a line get a red cross; then the dots regroup, clustering thickly around a signal and a turnout (`MAX GAP 1 KM`). Second half (animated, no whiteboard; owner 2026-10-16): whip pan to a 96 km Vadodara–Ahmedabad strip that fills with 2,872 amber tags (counter), then a lens magnifies 1 km: ≈ 30 tags. On-screen `MAX GAP 1 KM · 96 KM · 2,872 TAGS`.

D2_board_speed.title: 130 km/h = 36 m every second

cues.vo: At that speed, it covers about thirty six metres every single second.

D2_board_speed.spec: Real time, real scale: a trainset at 130 km/h passes a post every second, 36 m brackets light up, stopwatch and metres counter. Lower-third `130 KM/H · OUR CALCULATION 130 ÷ 3.6 ≈ 36 M/S`.

D3_board_freight.title: Freight ≈ 930 m (illustrative model)

cues.vo: Now picture a loaded goods train — five thousand tonnes at seventy five kilometres per hour. Its brakes build up slowly, and simple maths with fair guesses gives more than nine hundred metres to stop.

D3_board_freight.spec: Close tracking shot of a loaded goods train at 75 km/h pulls out (time-lapse) to a 1 km ruler: the brake application travels back along the wagons, amber zone `≈ 208 m` (brakes build up, 10 s) then crimson `≈ 723 m` under a speed curve, total bracket `≈ 930 m`; readouts km/h, metres, real seconds. Tag: OUR CALCULATION.

D4_network_size.title: The size of the job

cues.vo: So why isn't it on every track yet? Look at the size of the job. Indian Railways runs about sixty nine thousand route kilometres, and in March twenty twenty five it had about sixteen thousand diesel and electric engines.

D4_network_size.spec: Land-only India map (no political borders), carbon slate; the rail network draws in as thin grey lines across the country; counters land on the words: 69,439 ROUTE KM, then ≈ 16,000 LOCOS · MAR 2025. On-screen `69,439 ROUTE KM · ≈ 16,000 LOCOS · MAR 2025`. Rail lines: generic network density, labelled ILLUSTRATIVE if not from a real dataset.

D5_corridors.title: Kavach 4.0: 2,633 route km

cues.vo: By the end of July twenty twenty six, the newest Kavach was working on two thousand six hundred and thirty three route kilometres, on parts of the Delhi Mumbai and Delhi Howrah routes — two of the busiest in the country.

D5_corridors.spec: Same map; two corridors glow cyan: Delhi → Mumbai (label 1,423 KM GROUP) and Delhi → Howrah (1,210 KM GROUP); counter to 2,633. On-screen `KAVACH 4.0 · 2,633 RKM · 31 JUL 2026`.

D6_under_tenth.title: Plus the older version: under a tenth

cues.vo: Add the older version on about one thousand four hundred and sixty five kilometres in South Central Railway, and Kavach is still working on well under a tenth of the network.

D6_under_tenth.spec: Same map: a South Central Railway section glows in a second colour (amber-cyan); then a 10×10 grid (1 square = 1% of the network) lights ≈ 5.9% against a dashed ONE TENTH row. On-screen `VERSION 3.2 · 1,465 RKM · UNDER 10%`.

D7_funnel.title: Fitted ≠ working

cues.vo: And here's the trap in most headlines. Track fitted with equipment, seven thousand seven hundred and twenty six kilometres, engines fitted, six thousand two hundred and ninety, and track where work has only started, twenty one thousand seven hundred and ninety four kilometres... but fitted isn't working, and work started isn't protected.
cues.onscreen: FITTED 7,726 · LOCOS 6,290 · WORK STARTED 21,794 · FITTED ≠ WORKING

D7_funnel.spec: Three headline strips slide in, blurred except their numbers; then a funnel: WORK STARTED 21,794 (widest), FITTED 7,726, LOCOS 6,290, narrowing to the thin cyan WORKING stream; stamp `FITTED ≠ WORKING` lands on 'fitted isn't working'. On-screen `FITTED 7,726 · LOCOS 6,290 · WORK STARTED 21,794 · FITTED ≠ WORKING`.

D8_budget.title: Budget ₹1,112.57 cr → ₹1,673.19 cr

cues.vo: The money is moving too — the yearly Kavach budget rose from about one thousand one hundred crore rupees to about one thousand six hundred and seventy crore in twenty twenty five twenty six.

D8_budget.spec: Two precision bars rise with tabular counters: 2024–25 ₹1,112.57 CR, 2025–26 ₹1,673.19 CR. On-screen `₹1,112.57 CR (2024–25) → ₹1,673.19 CR (2025–26)`. Use latin-ext Inter for ₹.

D9_commissioning_loop.title: Money alone doesn't make it work

cues.vo: But money alone doesn't make it work. Every station's signalling data has to be checked, every engine type wired to its own brakes, the radio has to reach every yard, and then it's all tested and retested before a single kilometre is called working.

D9_commissioning_loop.spec: Flowchart drawn as a rail line: SURVEY → SIGNAL DATA → LOCO BRAKES → RADIO → TEST; a train token runs it, fails at TEST, loops back twice (FIX → RETEST), then reaches COMMISSIONED, which lights cyan. On-screen `COMMISSIONED`.

E1_family_group.title: Crash news blows up the family WhatsApp group

cues.vo: Then one morning there's news of a train crash, and by lunchtime your family WhatsApp group is on fire.

E1_family_group.spec: Realistic Android phone on a kitchen table (3D-ish, shallow depth of field); a generic news alert (no real outlet name) then a family group chat (generic names: Amma, Ravi Bava, Chinni…) with previews stacking fast and the unread counter climbing. Not WhatsApp branding: a generic green chat app.

E2_two_forwards.title: Two forwards

cues.vo: One forward says the government never bothered with safety, and another says India already has Kavach, so crashes should be impossible now.

E2_two_forwards.spec: Split screen of two forwarded messages (generic, 'Forwarded many times' style tag): left NO KAVACH? WHY?, right KAVACH = ZERO ACCIDENTS; on-screen `MYTH 1 · MYTH 2`. Keep the two cards: they return in E6.

E3_crack.title: Both forwards crack

cues.vo: Both forwards are playing with your fear — and both are missing what really happens on the track.

E3_crack.spec: The two forwards crack like glass on 'missing what really happens'; crash zoom through the crack into a dark night track bed (param `trackbed.mp4`, else a procedural ballast-and-rail plate with moonlight).

E4_not_an_app.title: Not an app, no overnight switch

cues.vo: Let's start with what Kavach actually is — because it isn't an app, and nobody can switch it on across India overnight.

E4_not_an_app.spec: A phone app icon labelled KAVACH dissolves into steel hardware parts; then a big industrial switch flips over a dim India map (land only) and nothing lights up. On-screen `NOT AN APP`.

E5_sil_half_story.title: SIL-4: half the story

cues.vo: The electronics are built to S-I-L four, the highest safety level in railway signalling. Some posts say that means Kavach can fail only once in a billion hours... that's only half the story, because it's a strict limit for each safety function of the electronics, not a promise that no train will ever crash.

E5_sil_half_story.spec: First half: a standards page (generic, styled like an EN document, no copied text) under a magnifier, the SIL band row highlighted; SIL-4 lands. Second half: a viral post card ONE FAILURE IN A BILLION HOURS slides in and a rubber stamp HALF THE STORY lands (.kav-stamp); then the SIL target lights one box in a small chain diagram, not the whole railway. On-screen `SIL-4 · HALF THE STORY`.

E6_beyond_evidence.title: Both forwards: beyond the evidence

cues.vo: So the forward saying Kavach would surely have saved Balasore, and the one saying it surely couldn't, are both going beyond the evidence.

E6_beyond_evidence.spec: The two forwards from E2 return side by side; each gets a stamp BEYOND THE EVIDENCE. On-screen `BEYOND THE EVIDENCE`.

E7_depends_setup.title: The 'always 15 km/h' claim

cues.vo: And what about the claim that Kavach always locks the speed at exactly fifteen kilometres per hour? Fifteen is the speed loco pilots must follow at failed signals — what Kavach enforces depends on its data and settings, so don't take that number as a promise.
cues.cite: [CCRS VIA INDIAN EXPRESS | JUL 2024 · PIB | FEB 2026]

E7_depends_setup.spec: A claim card 'KAVACH ALWAYS LOCKS 15 KM/H' (forward style) slides in; a speedometer graphic shows 15; then a stamp DEPENDS ON SET-UP lands. On-screen `DEPENDS ON SET-UP`.

E8_three_questions.title: Three questions before you share

cues.vo: One. When a Kavach forward lands in your family group, ask three questions before sharing it — is the number about fitted equipment or Kavach that's working, which date is it from, and was the problem a human mistake or wrong signalling data?
cues.onscreen: 1 · FITTED OR WORKING? · WHICH DATE? · HUMAN OR SIGNAL DATA?

E8_three_questions.spec: The forward from E2 on the phone; three question chips pop beside it on each question: FITTED OR WORKING? · WHICH DATE? · HUMAN OR SIGNAL DATA?; a small step marker 1 in a lower corner. On-screen `1 · FITTED OR WORKING? · WHICH DATE? · HUMAN OR SIGNAL DATA?`.

E9_pinned_question.title: Pinned comment question

cues.vo: Tell me in the comments: which route do you travel most, and do you know if Kavach is working on it yet?

E9_pinned_question.spec: A comment card (generic YouTube-like comment UI, no logo) in a lower corner over a slowly drifting land-only India rail map; text WHICH ROUTE DO YOU TRAVEL? On-screen `WHICH ROUTE DO YOU TRAVEL?`.
